note: Probe sentences for the Map of Harmony semantic view (#7129): what a page would SAY when it describes each kind of harmony or resonance, written as plain descriptive or first-person sentences, not topic labels. Several avoid the words harmony and sympathy on purpose, so the retrieval can find pages that describe the thing without naming it.

dimensions.label: Ratio and number
probes: When one string is half the length of the other, the two sound together as the same note an octave apart.
The pleasing intervals are made by the simplest numbers: two to one, three to two, four to three.
The proportions that please the ear are the same proportions found in the heavens and in the human body.
I divided the string on the monochord and measured where each consonance falls.
Numbers rule the sounds; the agreement of tones is nothing but the agreement of their measures.
The twelve pipes are generated one from another by adding and taking away a third of the length.

dimensions.label: Unlike things in one whole
probes: Things that are unlike must be bound together if they are to make one thing.
High and low, sharp and flat, opposed to each other, join into a single sound.
A good soup needs many flavours, salt and sour and bitter, each correcting the others.
If every voice sang the same note there would be no music, only a single sound.
Opposites fit together, and from things that differ comes the most beautiful order.
The ruler who only hears agreement is like someone who seasons water with water.

dimensions.label: Order and rank
probes: Each thing keeps its own place in the order of the world, from the highest heaven down to the earth.
The parts of the soul must be set in order, reason ruling and the passions obeying.
Heaven above and earth below each keep their station, and so the whole stands.
God disposed all things in measure, number and weight.
The planets move in their appointed circles, each at its own distance and speed.
When everything is in its proper rank, the household and the state are at peace.

dimensions.label: Balance and temperament
probes: Health is the right mixture of hot and cold, wet and dry, so that none prevails over the others.
When the humours are in their proper proportion the body is well; when one exceeds, sickness follows.
The wise person keeps to the middle way, neither too tight nor too slack, like a well-tuned string.
Joy and anger, sorrow and pleasure, when they arise in due measure, the mind is at peace.
Too much effort makes the mind restless and too little makes it lazy; strike the balance.
The breath, the fire and the water in the body must be kept in equal measure.

dimensions.label: Concord among people
probes: When the citizens are of one mind and share their goods, the city holds together.
Let the people agree with one another, so that the many nations live in peace.
Above all things, value peace among people and avoid quarrels and factions.
The council of many nations sits around one fire and decides with one mind.
Agreement among the churches can be restored if each side yields a little.
Different peoples with different customs can still live together under one law.

dimensions.label: Resonance and sympathy
probes: When one string is struck, another string tuned to the same note begins to sound by itself.
Things of the same kind call to one another and respond, as an echo answers a voice.
The lodestone draws iron to itself by a hidden affinity between them.
The ointment applied to the weapon heals the wound at a distance.
Two clocks hanging on the same beam soon swing together in step.
A paper figure placed on the string jumps when the matching note is played on another instrument.

dimensions.label: The feeling of consonance
probes: When I hear the two notes together I feel a sweetness, and the soul rests in it.
Some sounds pierce and grate on the ear, while others flow smoothly and delight it.
The listener is moved to tears when the melody matches the state of his heart.
Music enters the soul and changes the passions, making the angry calm and the sad joyful.
The spectator tastes the emotion as if it were his own, and his heart answers the performer's.
The ear judges at once what reason can explain only afterwards.

dimensions.label: The music of the heavens
probes: The heavens turn and their motion makes a sound that we do not hear because we have heard it since birth.
Each planet sounds its own note, and together they make a scale.
The souls before birth heard the music of the spheres and remember it when they hear song.
The world was made by music, and its parts are joined as the strings of a lyre.
The distances of the planets stand in the ratios of the musical intervals.
Pythagoras alone could hear the song of the stars.
